knowledgePoint.title: Finding the Parametric Equations of a Line

steps.markdown: Find the parametric equations of the straight line that passes through $P(1,-1,2)$ and is parallel to $v=⟨-2,3,-1⟩.$
steps.solution:
First, the vector equation of the line is 

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}+t\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \\ z\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-2t \\ 3t \\ -t\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \\ z\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}1-2t \\ -1+3t \\ 2-t\end{bmatrix},\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ Therefore, the parametric equations are:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=1-2t \\ y &=-1+3t \\ z &=2-t\end{aligned}\right.
$$

knowledgePoint.title: Finding the Parametric Equations of a Segment

steps.markdown:
Fill in the missing parts in the parametric equations below that describe all the points on the line segment $\overset{―}{PQ},$ where $P(1,9,-2)$ and $Q(-2,0,4).$
$x=$ $1-3t$ $t\in [$ {{field-1}} $,1]$
$y=$ $9-9t$
$z=$ {{field-2}}
steps.solution:
First, we need to find a direction vector that is parallel to the line passing through the given points. We can use the vector $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{PQ} \\  & =\overset{\to }{OQ}-\overset{\to }{OP} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ 0 \\ 4\end{bmatrix}-\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 9 \\ -2\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}-3 \\ -9 \\ 6\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the vector equation of the line is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 9 \\ -2\end{bmatrix}+t\begin{bmatrix}-3 \\ -9 \\ 6\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \\ z\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 9 \\ -2\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-3t \\ -9t \\ 6t\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \\ z\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}1-3t \\ 9-9t \\ -2+6t\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

To get the equations for the line segment, we take only $t\in [0,1].$ Notice that substitution of $t=0$ in the above equation gives the coordinates of $P$ and substitution of $t=1$ gives the coordinates of $Q.$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the line segment $\overset{―}{PQ}$ are the following:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=1-3t \\ y &=9-9t \\ z &=-2+6t\end{aligned}\right.\,\,t\in [0,1]
$$
